title: Drift & Coherence Review (run 3, trend vs the 2026-11-04 run 2): a small window (9 production LinearViewer commits + 4 SD commits; the parked-wait contract on both sides, the Stop-relay outcome table, Home/task-page parity) — verify the 11-04 ledger and open items
description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="drift-coherence-review" -->

**Drift & Coherence Review (run 3, trend vs the 11-04 run 2 edition)** is the trend-aware periodical (`drift-coherence` in `lib/periodicals.js`, series anchor LIN-369). It looks for code that is locally right while the system as a whole drifts apart. **This task is the review itself.** You write the report, mint the highest-severity follow-ups, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, and then conclude this task. Assume a cold hand-off: all you have is this description plus access to the repos and Linear.

This run is also read as the **top-down reading for the Survey research** (`docs/plans/survey/log.md` and `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That is context for what the numbers are used for, not extra scope: do not edit anything on that branch, and do not change what you report to fit it. If a finding bears on a place named in the place ledger, say so in one line and cross-link.

**Repos in remit:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour, primary), `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` (SD), and the runner kit inside Harbour (`lib/runner-kit/`, `docs/runner-prompt.md`). The cross-repo contract between them (runner contract table, halt, markers, consumer heartbeat, the model/effort/harness vocabulary, and the per-request usage records) is a seam no sibling review owns, so it belongs to this review.

**This is a small window, and a short report is a valid outcome.** The previous edition (`docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md`, LIN-4232, Done, PR #2277, merge `476d9ad4`) was written the evening of 2026-11-04. The window since its measured commits is 9 production commits in LinearViewer and 4 commits in SD (see Grounding). A mostly "unchanged / held" report with a close read of what moved is the expected shape. Do not widen the window, invent make-work, re-flag the 11-04 ledger as new, or pad the report to look like the previous edition. Say plainly how small the window was and what that did to the confidence of each "unchanged".

---

## Grounding (as found at mint time, 2026-11-05 \~08:00Z). Re-verify all of it; nothing here is a finding.

All numbers below are pre-mint probes from the minting agent. **Verify, don't quote.** Re-measure at your own HEAD and say if HEAD moved.

* **HEADs at mint.** LinearViewer `origin/main` = `2eb73ae07fb7297fc0fa057a6198aa8cbe901558` (LIN-4143, #2285, 06:00Z). simple-dispatcher `origin/main` = `07c88f7a338b3e19a01070775e1f4d4cfc91f040` (LIN-4233, #328, 2026-11-04 23:46Z).
* **The previous edition measured:** LinearViewer `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e` and SD `d8d186c07113d6e61e3489e38f1210d0b0624cad`; it ran the census with the guide `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` at `d7ceb373` (sha256 starting `e3194f52`) and recorded its evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-04-run2/`. Its own predecessor measured `5334c81a` / `502901c3`.
* **The window.**
  * LinearViewer `d7ceb373..2eb73ae0`: **11 commits**. Two are docs-only (`43dd0d64` Seams & Tangles run 6, `476d9ad4` the 11-04 run 2 report). Nine touch production (`lib routes public server.js`, 44 files, +1,430 / -363): LIN-4226 `c55f0fb3` (the cost read loads request records through a `requestSource`, LIN-4195 piece 4b), LIN-4234 `950113b1` (`usage-snapshot-intake` into INVENTORY; one source of collection names for both guards), LIN-4240 `279dcb0a` (`parseParkedWait` decides on the newest state-bearing entry), LIN-4241 `94195271` (settled-ruling guard, `409 ruling-settled`), LIN-4242 `ee8ec42e` (Waiting on you goes live: `home-waiting` fragment, shared keyed merge, one rulings tick), LIN-4243 `172f644a` (Home's Running and Up next follow the Waiting set), LIN-4151 `13fe24a0` (`/backlog` lead roots, one derivation for page and fold), LIN-4048 `c70b004c` (a finished task's page matches Home's run block), LIN-4143 `2eb73ae0` (the task page's ruling reads go through the live-run guard). **Added:** `lib/ruling-settled.js`, `lib/waiting-section.js`, `public/home-placement.js`. By `git diff`, `scripts/code-shape/` (guide and tools), `lib/runner-kit/` and `docs/runner-prompt.md` are **unchanged** in the window (verify), so the census can use one guide for both commits trivially; say so.
  * SD `d8d186c..07c88f7`: **4 commits** (`bf499a4` LIN-4218 one outcome table and one executor for every Stop relay; `796bc9d` LIN-4239 defer, blocked and failed post their status last; `580a5ea` LIN-4240 present-tense rewrite of the "until LIN-4240 lands" pointers; `07c88f7` LIN-4233 the present-tense rewrite of the `parseParkedWait` comments). Outside `test/`: `hook.js`, `opencode-runner.js` and `docs/module-map.md` (about +271 / -265; verify with `git diff --stat d8d186c 07c88f7 -- . ':!test'`).
* **First things to verify.** (a) The parked-wait marker is a cross-repo decision: Harbour's `parseParkedWait` (LIN-4240, `279dcb0a`) and SD's present-tense pointers (LIN-4240, LIN-4233) landed on both sides within hours; say whether it is now one contract with one owner, or two readers of one text format. (b) LIN-4218 collapses SD's Stop relays into one outcome table: re-read the 11-04 run 2 rows about the usage relay flag (`usage-relay-flag-partial`), the runner contract (`runner-contract-semantics-cross-repo`, still without a row for the two usage calls?) and the markers, against that change. (c) LIN-4241's `409 ruling-settled` and the `routes-error-envelope-fragmentation` row. (d) LIN-4048 / LIN-4143 / LIN-4242 / LIN-4243 against `home-next-answer-split` and `task-page-state-outside-owner`. (e) LIN-4234 and LIN-4226 against `usage-record-vocabulary-two-readers`, `cost-fold-partition-restated` and `lineage-identity-read-twins`.
* **Carry the ledger.** The 11-04 run 2 report's compact trend ledger is the list of rows: carry every row under its stable name with its severity and a delta, add a column for this edition, and retire a row only explicitly. Re-check the follow-up tickets that report names (for example LIN-4210, 4156, 4157, 4158, 3822, 3823, 3449, 4195) with `GET $HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE/api/proxy/issues/<id>`, and say by diff, per row, not by assumption; a file touched without being consolidated is a sharper delta than "unchanged". Do not choose an answer to a question the report marks as John's ruling (for example the halt cold-cache row, LIN-4210/LIN-3024).
* **Census tool and readings to reproduce.** `scripts/code-shape/census-review.mjs` (documented in `scripts/code-shape/README.md`); the previous run's readings and exact scope pattern are in its report and `_evidence-2026-11-04-run2/`. Run it at `2eb73ae0` against `d7ceb373` with one guide for both, record both full commits and the guide file's hash, and say how the groups moved. Re-measure the import graph the same way (nodes, edges, SCCs and members, upward edges, route->route).
* **Report convention:** `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/` where the previous edition kept it (check). Today is 2026-11-05, so use `drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05.md` and `_evidence-2026-11-05/` if those names are free, and do not overwrite any 11-04 file. PR and commit convention: `LIN-NNNN: <summary> (#PR)`; `ci-success` must be green before merging (`CLAUDE.md`). `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` needs a comment on this task citing a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, plus the three second-read fields in one comment body, before Done.
* **Siblings and the seams between them.** **Seams & Tangles** (run 7, minted alongside this task; its predecessor `seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04-run6.md`, LIN-4231) owns area-level knots, change coupling and route->route; **Code Quality** (`code-quality-review-2026-11-04.md`) owns function size; **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-11-04.md`) owns churn. Do not re-flag what they own; cross-link.

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* and fold it in. Examples to check: the runner side of the parked-wait contract (Harbour `parseParkedWait`, LIN-4240, against SD's present-tense rewrites LIN-4240/LIN-4233 and the status-last ordering of LIN-4239); SD's single Stop-relay outcome table (LIN-4218) against Harbour's reading of the same markers and `lib/runner-kit/contract.json`; the new `409 ruling-settled` code (LIN-4241) against the routes' error-envelope convention; the Home and task-page run blocks (LIN-4048) and ruling reads (LIN-4143) for a decision now held in two places or consolidated into one; the shared keyed merge and `home-waiting` fragment (LIN-4242/4243) against the other live-update fragments; the cost read's `requestSource` (LIN-4226) against `request-usage-*`. A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Read the 11-04 run 2 report (`drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md`) in full (its Headline, Method, Findings, Cross-repo contract verdicts, Sibling hand-offs, Classes and bounds, Follow-ups, For John, Ticket trend, Adversarial second-read and Compact trend ledger), then the 11-04 and 11-03 reports as background. Frame every finding as a delta against the 11-04 run 2 edition: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot.
* **Run the review.** This review works at the cross-cutting altitude (locally right, globally drifting), distinct from the per-module Code Quality Review; do not re-flag what it owns. Use the repo's own conventions as the reference, introducing no new tooling. Assess: *duplication* (a decision re-implemented where one shared implementation is canonical; coincidental similarity is fine); *convention fragmentation* (competing patterns where one is canonical, flag the outliers); *dependency direction* (imports against the repo's own layering, for example a core module reaching into a route); and the *cross-repo contract* (Harbour <-> SD <-> runner kit). Name the concrete cost a change would hit, not a style preference; no cosmetic churn. Do not find repeated decisions by eye: run the committed census tool (above) at HEAD and at the commit the previous report measured, with one area guide for both runs; record the full commits. Give every `mustRule` group one ruling in a compact table: real (the one place the decision should live and why, or both claimants and your pick), borderline or noise, with a one-line reason; a ruling is your finding, not a question to anyone. List the table groups in one compact table, no ruling. Prose and follow-up tasks only for real groups and for changes since the previous edition. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report.** The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found; finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work, and a clean result is a genuine outcome. Ground each finding against the source at HEAD, not prior prose. Close the report with the compact trend ledger: every row of the 11-04 run 2 ledger under its stable name, with its severity and its delta against the 11-04 run 2 edition, plus any new rows.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar, and in a window this small it usually will). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state (the 11-04 edition parented its follow-up under LIN-3449 with kind:follow-up; follow that if a ticket is minted). **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (the 11-04 run 2 edition's "Considered and not minted" list and its search phrases are the model); if one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating: the Backlog holds the unmoved Drift-family tickets the 11-04 run 2 report lists (check which have moved) (`coherence-loop-stalled`), so weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs). Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets in either repo, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.

- Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/40557e9f47c30d50a52c1e2a788e9d47a6feb3e1/docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05.md
- PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2288 (merge `40557e9f`)
- Evidence: `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05-drift/`. The `-drift` suffix is there because Seams run 7 took `_evidence-2026-11-05/` first.

**Adversarial second-read:** Tier 2 (a fresh-context sub-agent). Full answer: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/40557e9f47c30d50a52c1e2a788e9d47a6feb3e1/docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05.md#adversarial-second-read

Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE
Differed from top finding: YES
Disposition: fixed in place

**Window:** small. LinearViewer `d7ceb373..2eb73ae0` had 11 commits (9 production, 44 files) and SD `d8d186c..07c88f7` had 4 (3 non-test files). The guide, the runner kit and the runner prompt did not change. The census under one guide reads 566 / 105 `mustRule` / 309 table; all 105 groups are ruled (34 real, 29 borderline, 42 noise). The import graph has the same two SCCs, 0 upward edges, and 53 route→route edges.

**Findings, by severity (delta vs 11-04 run 2):**
1. MEDIUM-HIGH, unchanged: `resume-model-effort-cross-repo` (LIN-4156) and `credential-decision-multiplicity` (LIN-3822).
2. MEDIUM, unchanged:
   - marker vocabulary across repos;
   - `halt-poll-cold-cache-fail-open` (LIN-4210, John's ruling; not chosen);
   - `runner-contract-semantics-cross-repo`: 38 vs 34 rows and still no usage row, although LIN-4218 now puts the usage flush first in SD's Stop order;
   - `halt-word-map-copies`;
   - `run-page-identity-scrape`.
3. MEDIUM, improved: `home-next-answer-split` (partly, LIN-4151) and `coherence-loop-stalled` (LIN-4234 and LIN-4151 Done; 16 open, 14 unmoved).
4. **New, LOW-MEDIUM: `parked-wait-text-cross-repo`.** SD writes one park status for 4 wait kinds, and Harbour reads 1 of them as parked (`PARKED_WAIT_HINT`). Neither side has a contract row, and the only test that checks it is SD's system tier, outside SD CI. Its home is LIN-2258.
5. LOW-MEDIUM: `live-anchor-old-home-alive` improved (LIN-4143). `decision-stamp-classifier-copies` was touched without being consolidated.
6. **New, LOW:**
   - `ruling-settled-row-predicate-inline`: the settled check went from 2 inline sites to 5 (LIN-4241). No ticket names it, and it was not minted (see the report).
   - `error-code-case-split`: `ruling-settled` is the only kebab-case error code.
   - `waiting-standing-comment-residue`: three window comments contradict the code. One of them came from the second-read.
   - `request-source-guard-copies`: three inline loader checks beside `requireRequestUsageLoader`, found by the second-read.
7. LOW, improved: `usage-snapshot-prose-residue` (1 of 9 files).
8. Borderline: `reply-effect-default-split` (new) and `completeness-precedence-restated`.
9. **Resolved:** `erasure-inventory-lockstep-gap` (LIN-4234).

**Ledger:** all 124 run 2 rows carried (102 unchanged, 17 held, 4 improved, 1 resolved) plus 6 new, for 130. None was retired.

**Follow-ups:** none minted. The searches and reasons are in the report. Observation: LIN-2739's problem was fixed by LIN-4241 (`dispatch-store.js:3841-3842`), but the ticket is still Backlog.

**Autopilot run summary (stepper, session `5e7b27ec`)**

The work ran as five beats in one worker session (`ROOT` `756b5d69`), all `kind: research`, following the LIN-4232 precedent.

1. **Ground and re-measure.** HEADs had not moved since mint (LinearViewer `2eb73ae0`, SD `07c88f7`). The census guide sha256 is `e3194f52`, the same file at both commits. The census reproduced 11-04 run 2 exactly. I checked the ticket states against the tracker.
2. **Seams and unlisted scope.** Items (a)–(f) were ruled. The 105 `mustRule` groups came out as 34 real, 29 borderline and 42 noise. Three new findings were added, and the tickets it cited exist as described.
3. **Write the report and open the PR.** This beat wedged for about 90 minutes: the follow-up arrived while the worker's context was being compacted. One liveness nudge resumed it. It produced PR #2288 at `88ee6733`, with all 7 checks green and every file under `docs/reviews/`.
4. **Follow-ups and second-read.** No ticket was minted; the one candidate is LOW, and the reasons and search phrases are in the report. The Tier 2 second-read (a fresh-context sub-agent) returned AGREE, Differed from top finding YES, fixed in place. The new head `6b0a273f` was green.
5. **Merge, gate comment and Done.** PR #2288 was squash-merged as `40557e9f`. The `Tests` run 42010838532 succeeded on that SHA. Comment `6ec0a0ed` carries the three fields and the report URL, and the task moved to Done.

**What I verified myself:** the PR state is MERGED, `main` CI is green on `40557e9f`, the [report blob](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/40557e9f47c30d50a52c1e2a788e9d47a6feb3e1/docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05.md) returns 200, LIN-4250 is Done, and the gate comment holds all three fields in one body.

**What's left / notes:**
- There was no separate `review` / `close-out` stage. The task description makes the second-read the review and tells the task to merge its own docs-only report PR, so that is what happened.
- The evidence lives in `_evidence-2026-11-05-drift/` because Seams run 7 had already used `_evidence-2026-11-05/`.
- Not run: SD's system test tier.
- LIN-2739 looks already fixed by LIN-4241; the report notes this, but the ticket itself was not touched.
